Nymphet – The Risqué Novels is vol. 2 in a compilation of erotic short stories / fiction produced between late 1983 and 1984, slated as 'Girlie Erotica'. Edited by Shinji Nakamura under the imprint Bungei Sensen (文芸戦線), also associated with the circle FAKS Yōseikyō Kishidan (FAKS 妖精郷騎士団). Bungei Sensen itself is a play off of the actual Bungei Sensen, a Japanese proletariat journal that ran from the late Taisho period to the early Showa period.

this volume comprises of both derivative and original works, both with a lolicon and shotacon theme, drawing on derivative parody works based on Aura Battler Dunbine and Round Vernian Vifam. In particular, this work has a heavy focus on S & M and generally taboo theme, though in context, the novels are quite softcore.

Published on November 1, 1984 and distributed at Comiket 27, the volume was produced under strict deadlines and clear submission guidelines. Contributors were instructed to submit B5-sized illustrations in black ink only, with both original and derivative works permitted; however, the erotic orientation of the publication was explicitly prioritized. Compensation was standardized, with contributors receiving a complimentary copy upon participation.

"For illustrations, use B5 paper and black ink only. Colored inks are not allowed. Either primary or secondary (original or derivative) works are fine. However, since this is essentially an erotic-oriented publication, please keep that aspect in mind… to put it simply.

For contributors’ copies, we will offer a fixed payment. Those who submit even once will receive a complimentary copy. Bye."

The publication situates itself within the collaborative ecology of early 1980s doujin culture though is not a goudoushi in a traditional sense and seems to have been mainly funded by Nakamura himself. Nakamura’s appeal for readers to support Group Saturos (グループサチュロス), particularly its Top Taste imprint, suggests interlinked networks among these publishing circles, including possible proximity to the Cheer Up! and LOUDNESS imprints.

Retrospectively, works of this kind have been associated with the so-called “forbidden books” phenomenon: publications that combined lolicon-inflected themes with aesthetic strategies derived from pin-up and idol culture. While Nymphet participates in this broader milieu, it also demonstrates a strong formal influence from science fiction coterie magazines and small-press literary journals, particularly in its structure. The circle’s later imprint name itself alludes to The Knight of Fairyland (Hayakawa Bunko), underscoring its intertextual positioning between commercial SF literature and underground erotic production.

★Additionals:

Some contributors, such as Yam and Sin, were directly involved with the Hideo Azuma camp and were regular contributors to Bishoujo Aifukakai No Tail (美少女愛好会 シッポがない).

★From Nakamura:

Hitorigoto (Muttering to Myself) …or Afterword

Ahh, what should I do about the manuscript!! I’m in trouble. It’s already past the deadline. The printing cost is 30,000 yen…

I’ve been busy mostly with other things, so I’ll write about something different. Anyway, coloring was really difficult. Even typing this takes time.

This time, we were helped by Jitsukawa-san. I’m very grateful. We weren’t going to make it in time for Comiket, and originally we were supposed to go sell this volume in Tokyo.

Well…

Among erotic doujinshi, this one is rather unusual. It’s not text-centered, but one of the first attempts at making a doujinshi focused mainly on erotic fiction, isn’t it? However, there are many problems. First, it tends to become formulaic. Erotic fiction often ends up with similar patterns, and depending on the situation, you have no choice but to vary the presentation. My own erotic stories have mostly been magical-girl themed, and the pattern is starting to show. I feel like new characters are necessary. Also, since there’s no compensation for submissions, this book continues in a very direct, almost self-funded way. Anyway, our goal is to “have fun.”

So with that said, this issue once again contains plenty of interesting material. Please continue to support works like TOP-TASTE by Hayashi Shōten. Well then, until we meet again.
